text: LATEST OUTRAGE.

label: paragraph_title
text: PIRATES SEIZE B. & S. STEAMER.

label: text
text: “Sunning” Set Ablaze.

label: text
text: REPORTED STERN RESISTANCE— “SOMEONE WOUNDED.”

label: text
text: Having been pirated and set afire by the pirates in consequence, it is thought, of the determined resistance put up by the officers, the China Navigation (Butterfield and Swire) steamer "Sunning," a coastal vessel engaged on the run between Shanghai and Hong Kong, was discovered in the early hours of this morning by H.M.S. "Blue bell" off Chelang Point, between Amoy and Hong Kong, in distress.

label: text
text: "Wireless messages briefly recording this fact and that two other China Navigation vessels are standing by to render assistance, in addition to H.M.S. "Bluebell," were received in Hong Kong this morning.

label: text
text: The “Sunning” was on her way from Shanghai to Hong Kong with European passengers on board and the usual coastal cargo. The vessel left Amoy yesterday morning.

label: text
text: No news of any casualties has been received, beyond the brief reference to someone having been wounded, nor is it possible to tell at the moment the extent of the damage.

label: text
text:
When discovered, the upper works of the ship were afire, but determined efforts were being made to get the flames under control.
As soon as the news was received in Hong Kong this morning, the Taikoo Dock tug was despatched to the scene to assist and to tow the disabled vessel to Hong Kong, should it be found necessary.

label: text
text:
The value of the haul made by the pirates is not as yet known—in fact, particulars of any sort as to the piracy are lacking, but it is thought that the pirates booked as passengers at Shanghai.
When the "Sunning" was discovered by H.M.S. "Bluebell," which was on its way to Swatow from Hong Kong, the pirates had made good their escape.

label: text
text: Later: It is understood that the flames have been subdued. Owing to the heavy seas running, which has rendered access to the "Sunning" by vessels standing by extremely difficult, also to the fact that the wireless-apparatus of the "Sunning" has been damaged, very few details can at present be given. It is understood authentically that "some-one has been wounded" but that no deaths have has yet been reported.

label: text
text: The information at present received has been by means of signals from the damaged vessel and that accounts for its bareness of detail.

label: text
text: The two B. and S. vessels standing by are the “Kaying,” proceeding northwards from Hong Kong, and the “Suiyang,” proceeding southwards.

label: text
text: The "Sunning" will not arrive in Hong Kong today. The scene of the piracy and fire is some 80 miles distance from Hong Kong and the heavy seas render towing impracticable at present.

label: paragraph_title
text: THEY KILLED HIM.

label: paragraph_title
text: GIRLS PATHETIC APPEAL IN COURT.

label: paragraph_title
text: A VILLAGE FEUD

label: text
text: "They killed my father; is not this court going to recess the grievances of my father."

label: text
text: Bursting into sobs under the cross-examination of counsel, the young daughter of the man killed at Taikiu village, New Territories, following a dispute between inhabitants of that village and those of Wang Chau, addressed the above appeal to the court.

label: text
text: Three men who are being tried on a charge of manslaughter before Mr. Justice Wood are being defended by Mr. C. G. Albaster K.C.

label: text
text: In the course of this morning's hearing, Mr. Alabaster put it to the daughter of the man killed that deceased had been at the head of an opposing faction at the time he met his death. Counsel suggested that what happened was that two men from Wong Chau pursued three women who had been gathering pig fodder from a padi field, that deceased and a number of other men from Taikiu went out and attacked them, and that one of the prisoners had then seized the spear that the deceased held and had laid about him in self defence.

label: text
text: This the witness denied, and said that there was a considerable body of men from Wong Chuu, all of whom were armed. Four of them attacked her father when he remonstrated with them for chasing the women.

label: text
text: In reply to further questions, witness denied that the spear-was one her father kept as a relic of the days before the establishing of police stations in the New Territories and when villagers had to defend themselves. Her father was not armed at the time he was attacked.

label: text
text: The Tune is proceeding.

label: text

text: STOLEN JEWELS

label: paragraph_title
text: REPORTED FIND ON ARRESTED MAN.

label: text
text: A NOTORIOUS BURGLAR?

label: text
text: Believed to be the perpetrator of a number of the major burglaries that have occurred in the Colony during the past few months, Ho Leung, alias Ho Yue, 22, unemployed, was arrested outside St. Paul's Hostel on Saturday morning, it is said, and was found in possession of a quantity of jewellery, the property of Mrs. Beecher, treasurer of St. Paul's Hostel, Dr. Y. S. Wan and Mr. P. S. Wong, also of St. Paul's Hostel.

label: text
text: The Police are actively engaged upon the investigation of a number of cases of burglary which, it is alleged, have been traced to the arrested man. These include the theft of jewellery and other valuables which took place at the residence of M. G. Grimble, the well-known loc: J broker, at Brank-Home Towers last week.

label: text
text:
When the accused was brought before Major C. Willson at the Central Magistracy this morning, Inspector Carey asked for a remand as the Police wished to investigate the matter further.
His Worship remanded the accused in custody for a week.

label: paragraph_title
text: GUILTY KNOWLEDGE

label: paragraph_title
text: JUNK MASTER AND REVOLVER.

label: text
text: A junk master appeared this morning before Mr. J. H. B. Nihill, at the Kowloon Magistracy, charged with unlawful possession of a res-volver and several rounds of ammunition.

label: text
text: Mr. J. Remedios, who appeared for the defence, said "defendant had a licence to possess three rifles, but did not have one for this revolver. He said that three Chinese soldiers were passengers of the boat from Ping, Hoi to Hong Kong and that these men had left the revolver in the junk." He pointed out that to convict the defendant, the police had to prove "defendant's" guilty knowledge.

label: paragraph_title
text: CANTON TRADE.

label: text
text:
The police informed the bench that defendant made a statement to the police saying that the three soldiers had left the revolver in his possession, which proved according to the police his "knowledge of its existence" in his junk.
Defendant was fined $75.

label: paragraph_title
text:
Shirping Boycott
Ceases.

label: paragraph_title
text: CARGO ON THE MOVE.

label: text
text: Normal Relations Likely

label: text
text: The "new" boycott is rapidly nearing its end and complete for small relations between Cantons and Hong Kong should be restored within a few weeks.

label: text
text: The Canton Government, it will be recalled, promised to call the boycott off on October 10. Canton kept its word, and the pickets retired.

label: text
text: Then came the new boycott. This has never received official recognition nor—as far as is known—any encouragement or help.

label: text
text: Two bodies were mainly active in the new boycott but a third was “interested.” Ex-Heamen agitators who wanted their jobs back and the Transport. Union directed “attention to passengers and traffic while the Economic Severance Association made investigation as to stocks of British goods in Canton.

label: text
text: As foreshadowed by reports published in the "China Mail" on Saturday, and confirmed yesterday; better counsels have now prevailed. The Transport men now want to work and will handle cargo from Hong Kong. The ex-seamen pickets have been pacified and have abandoned their "peaceful blockade."

label: text
text: The merchants who supported the Severance Committee are not nearly so prominent as the more sensible who have argued that it is treason against the Koumintang to hinder the resumption of communications, that being now the policy of the Party.

label: text
text: From the outset, leading Chinese traders who have been in touch with the "China Mail" and whose views have been given prominence in these columns were confident that the strike, boycott and blockade would be entirely settled, as all parties had to retain the goodwill of the Nationalist Government and the Government was in favour of trade.

label: text
text: Although the amount of cargo going up this morning (following the cancellation of the transport boycott) was comparatively small, the "China Mail" can give only the same reason as before, viz. pessimism and the usual desire to wait a few days to see the outcome.

label: text
text: The thin end of the wedge has now been inserted by those who wish to trade, and there is no reason why all ships, including British, should not be working again at Canton in a week or two.

label: text
text: The attention of malcontents having been diverted from the Steamboat Co.'s wharves in Canton, it is now predicted that cargo-boats, coolies, etc., will not be reluctant to discharge and load British vessels at Canton.

label: text
text: Further news from Kongmoon is that the industrial dispute there was settled by the good offices of the Customs brokers. The coolies got one side of the business and the boatmen the other. Shipments are now moving freely between that port and Hong Kong and Kongmoon merchants are looking forward to a satisfactory settlement when the winter solstice comes round on Dec. 22.

label: paragraph_title
text: COAL HOPES.

label: paragraph_title
text: Settlement Almost Certain.

label: text
text: SOUTH WALES VOTES.

label: text
text: Change From United Front

label: text
text: The first votes taken in the coal-fields have been in favour of accepting the terms proposed by the Government for a settlement. Such decisions were reached at meetings of miners at Clydach Valo, Blaenavon, Garndiffalth, and Abertillery in South Wales.

label: text
text: The Miners' Councils of Yorkshire and Warwickshire have also decided by a big majority in favour of acceptance.

label: text
text: It is noteworthy that in South Wales the men have preserved a more united front than in any other coalfield, and that the South Wales representatives voted for rejection of the Government proposals at the Delegate Conference held in London last Saturday.

label: text
text:
The favourable decisions now re-corded by the above mentioned South Wales districts may therefore, without undue optimism, be taken as indicating the probability of the settlement being accepted, not only in South Wales, but generally throughout the country.
Meanwhile, the number of miners returning to work maintains its steady daily increase. To-day's increase, is 7,442, bringing the total men at work up to 338,153.—British Wireless Service.

label: paragraph_title
text: A Majority Certain

label: text
text: Reports from a number of fields indicate that a majority will be obtained for acceptance of the Government's plan.

label: text
text: The South Wales Miners' Federation has decided to accept the terms. "as a matter of loyalty to the Miners' Federation."

label: text
text: The Lancashire and Cheshire Federation endorsed the action of the conference federation delegates in supporting acceptance.

label: text
text: The Yorkshire Miners' Council met, presided over by Mr. Herber Smith.

label: text
text: No statement was made after the meeting, but it is believed the proposals were overwhelmingly adopted.

label: text
text: Over thirty collieries are already working in Northumberland. Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: Earlier Messages.

label: text
text: Extraordinary interest prevailed in a crowded police court at Renishaw, Derbyshire, when there were four summonses charging the M.P., Mr. Kirkwood, with breaking the emergency regulations in the course of speeches in Derbyshire villages on November 2.

label: text
text: The case was adjourned for a week on Mr. Kirkwood's application for time to prepare his defence. "In view of the great constitutional principles involved."—. Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text:
The Government Plan.
Ruxby Nov.

label: text
text:
The present week is generally expected to see the termination of the coal dispute: The miners' district associations are deciding whether to accept, as recommended by their delegates conference, the proposals for a settlement presented by the Government. All districts must decide before Thursday, and the results will be presented at the delegates' conference on Friday.
Already in South Wales, it Elaenavon, Abertillery and Garn-diffath, the miners have voted in favour of acceptance, and other districts are expected to provide at least a majority for this course.
The Government proposals are designed to secure a standard form of agreement in every coalfield. Anything like exact equality is not the aim of the plan, but it perpetuates common principles and common factors for calculation of district wage rates, and virtually establishes a national minimum. It accures the working in the districts of machinery for regulation of wages above that minimum in accordance with the state of prosperity of the industry. It allows of some elasticity in the fixing of profits, and it assures continuance of the subsistence allowance. It provides for agreements of duration of not less than three years.
The standard agreement makes no reference to the length of the work

label: paragraph_title
text: CHINA PERILS.

label: paragraph_title
text: Protecting British Subjects.

label: text
text: HOME GOVERNMENT'S STANEL

label: text
text: In the House of Commons, Sir H. Harry Britain asked whether any effective form of co-operation existed between the Powers interested in the protection of the lives and property of their nationals in China.

label: text
text:
The Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs, Sir Austen Chamberlain, replied that the co-operation of the Powers was always practised as far as means permitted, but such co-operation was not subject to formal agreement.
Sir Austen Chamberlain added in answer to a supplementary question, that practical co-operation had been secured quite recently.

label: text
text: Mr. H. W. Looker asked for an assurance that the British Government would not hesitate to take any steps necessary, not merely to ensure the protection and security of British subjects, but to ensure British rights of property and other British rights were not interfered with.

label: text
text: Sir Austen Chamberlain said that the Government would continue to do its best to protect British lives and interests.

label: text
text: Sir Austen Chamberlain told Mr. C. P. Trevelyan that the new British Minister, Mr. Miles Lampson, was proceeding to Peking.—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: "A SOWS EAR."

label: text
text: CONSTABLE WHO SLEPT ON DUTY.

label: text
text: MAKING AN EXAMPLE

label: text
text: A Cantonese, lukong, P.C.C128, appeared before Mr. R. E. Lind-sell at the Central Magistracy this morning in answer to a charge of sleeping on duty.

label: text
text: Mr. C. G. Perdue, Assistant Director of Criminal Intelligence, conducted the case on behalf of the Police, and Mr. S. H. Loseby defended the accused.

label: text
text: His Worship asked Mr. Perdue whether it was not unusual to bring a man to the Magistracy for sleeping on duty. In reply, Mr. Perdue stated that the defendant had already been punished departmentally three times this year for the same offence. The Captain Superintendent of Police took a serious view of the case as the man was the only lukong at the police station at the time. A sergeant had found him there asleep. He had been instructed to press for a severe term of imprisonment without the option of a fine.

label: text
text: Mr. Loseby said that he had examined the defendant at some length. He was obviously no use as a police officer and, in his opinion, it was a case of trying to make a silk purse out of a sow's ear. He would ask the Bench to make an example of the man and no more.

label: text
text: The Magistrate! Six weeks lard labour.
